p: Thinking of a family session? It can be a cracking day out for older children, but there are a few things to sort before you go. Junior drivers have to meet age and height minimums, and junior sessions may run at different times to adult ones, so check TeamSport's website for what's available and book the right slot.

Talk your youngsters through what to expect beforehand: the helmet, the briefing, the flags. Kids who know what's coming tend to settle in quickly and enjoy it more. It also helps to remind them it's about improving their own lap times, not just beating big brother.

If you've got non-racing little ones with you, plan something for them too. Bristol is brilliant for families. We The Curious on the harbourside is a hands-on science centre that keeps kids busy for hours, M Shed is a free museum about the city's history, and Brunel's SS Great Britain is a fantastic day out for anyone with an interest in ships.
Leave a cushion of time between attractions. Bristol traffic can be slow, and parking near the harbourside fills up quickly at weekends, so give yourselves a buffer before your race slot.
Finish with a walk up to Clifton Suspension Bridge for one of the best views in the West Country.
